decisive_items: right foot drop (tibialis anterior, extensor hallucis longus, flexor hallucis longus, and peroneus longus 1/5; left side 4/5)
Repeat peroneal conduction studies failed to elicit an evoked myogenic potential
response.rationale: Lumbosacral plexopathy best explains the combination of peroneal and tibial innervated muscle weakness (foot drop plus flexor hallucis longus) and absent Achilles reflexes, while peroneal neuropathy alone cannot account for tibial involvement or reflex loss. MRI showing no significant nerve-root compression argues against radiculopathy.

rejected.why: Initial diagnosis but progression and lack of new compression on MRI make it unlikely as the cause of deterioration.
Arteriography showed no significant vascular lesions, ruling out peripheral artery disease.
MRI demonstrated no significant nerve-root or cord compression, contradicting radiculopathy.
Peripheral neuropathy is too broad; the focal and progressive pattern with specific nerve involvement suggests a more localized lesion.
Arteriography was normal and no systemic vasculitic features are present, making vasculitic neuropathy unlikely.
